# Containr

> Self-hosted Docker PaaS — deploy and manage containerized apps, databases, cron jobs and preview environments. Operable by humans (web UI) and agents (API / CLI / MCP) through one contract.

Base URL: `https://<host>/api/v1`. OpenAPI: `docs/api/openapi.yaml`.

## Access (pick one)

- **API**: `Authorization: Bearer <pat>` — create a PAT in Settings → Access Tokens or `containr tokens create`. Scopes: `read` (GET/HEAD/OPTIONS only), `write` (everything but admin routes), `admin` (requires platform-admin owner).
- **CLI**: `containr auth login --api-url <url>` (or `--token cnp_…`), then e.g. `containr projects list --json`, `containr up`. Global flags: `--json`, `--yes`, `--profile`, `--idempotency-key`.
- **MCP**: run `containr-mcp` over stdio with `CONTAINR_API_URL` + `CONTAINR_TOKEN` env (or CLI profile). ~60 tools mirroring the API; destructive tools require `confirm: true`.

## Conventions

- **Errors**: `{"error": "msg", "code": "MACHINE_CODE"}`. Codes: `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `INVALID_TOKEN`, `FORBIDDEN`, `ADMIN_REQUIRED`, `SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT`, `NOT_FOUND`, `VALIDATION`, `CONFLICT`, `INTERNAL`, `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`, `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`, `NOT_CANCELLABLE`.
- **Idempotency**: send `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` on POSTs — the first response replays for 24h; concurrent duplicates get 409. Always safe to send.
- **Pagination**: `?limit=` + `?cursor=` (pass `pagination.next_cursor` verbatim; legacy `?page=` also works). Invalid cursors fall back to page 1.
- **Deployments**: serialized per service — a deploy on a busy service returns `status: queued` and runs when the active one finishes. `POST /deployments/{id}/cancel` drops queued (`200 cancelled`) or aborts running (`202 cancelling`) work. `no_cache: true` on create disables the Docker layer cache. `PUT /services/{id}/variables` accepts `redeploy: true` to apply env changes to running containers.
- **Volumes**: service mounts via `PUT /services/{id}` `volumes: [{type: volume|bind, source, target, read_only}]` — replaces the whole list (`[]` clears), applied on next deploy. `GET /admin/volumes` inventories node volumes with `in_use` flags; `DELETE /admin/volumes/{name}` removes unused ones (admin).
- **Domains**: multiple hostnames per service via `GET|POST /services/{id}/domains`, `DELETE /services/{id}/domains/{domain_id}`, `POST …/{domain_id}/default` (mirrors `services.domain`). `GET /services/{id}/domains/check` returns `ok|wrong-target|pending` per domain vs `app_settings.public_ip`/`PUBLIC_IP`. `PUT` `maintenance_mode` redirects all traffic to `GET /maintenance` (needs `base_url`/`BASE_URL` setting); `basic_auth: [{username,password}]` stores bcrypt htpasswd and gates the route — responses return usernames only.
- **Builders & resources**: service field `builder` = `auto|railpack|nixpacks|dockerfile|static` (auto detects; static builds assets with `static_build_cmd` and serves `static_dir` via nginx:80). `cpu`/`memory` are hard caps; `cpu_reserve`/`memory_reserve` are soft reservations (CPU shares / MemoryReservation) — empty string clears. `app_settings.default_cpu`/`default_memory` set instance defaults; `app_settings.capacity_policy=block` rejects deploys exceeding node memory (default `warn`).
- **Clone & move**: `POST /services/{id}/clone` `{name?, project_id?, environment?}` copies config, volumes, domains, access gates, and variables (secret ciphertext verbatim; clone starts stopped). `POST /services/{id}/move` `{project_id}` re-parents a service — both require ownership of source and target; name conflicts → `CONFLICT`. Cloned domains are verbatim copies: the same hostname on two services makes routing ambiguous.
- **Registries**: `GET|POST /registries`, `PUT|DELETE /registries/{id}` — owner-scoped private-image pull credentials, encrypted at rest, never returned (`has_password` signals presence). `host` matched against the image reference on image deploys (`docker.io` for Docker Hub; scheme/case normalized). Empty `password` on update keeps the stored credential.
- **External databases**: `POST /databases/register-external` (probes first; `{name,type,host,port,database,username,password,ssl}`), `POST /databases/test-connection` (ad-hoc probe → `{ok,latency_ms,error}`), `POST /databases/{id}/test-connection` (re-probe with stored credentials). Rows carry `provider:"external"` + `external{host,port,database,username,has_password,ssl}`; passwords encrypted at rest, never returned. Lifecycle actions and backups reject external rows — no container exists.
- **Public DB port**: managed databases bind `127.0.0.1` by default; `public_port:true` on create or `PUT /databases/{id} {public_port}` binds `0.0.0.0`. Toggling recreates the container — the data volume persists.
- **Backup targets**: S3-compatible destinations (`/backup-targets` CRUD + `POST /backup-targets/{id}/test`). Endpoints/buckets are probed before storing; keys encrypted at rest (`has_credentials` only). Assign via `PUT /databases/{id} {backup_target_id}` — empty string clears; external databases reject assignment. Managed backups stay local; a copy ships to `[prefix/]databases/<db-id>/<archive>` and rows expose `remote:true`. Restore prefers the local archive and falls back to the remote object. Deleting a target is refused (409) while databases reference it.
- **Identifiers**: all ids are UUIDs. Tokens: `cnp_` user PATs, `cagt_` agent onboarding tokens.

## Core objects

`projects` → `services` (git/app deploys) → `deployments`; plus `databases`, `templates`, `cron-jobs`, `variables`, `volumes`, `domains`, `registries`, `preview-environments`, `nodes`, `scaling`, `security`, `gateway`, `admin`, `notifications`, `user/tokens`.
